messages:
maya: Heads-up: seeing a spike of ECC/Xid errors on a small subset of us-west GPU nodes, one node crossed our auto-quarantine thresholds. infra-bot just fired an alert.
infra-bot: ALERT 1778005123: node=gpu-node-7 region=us-west errors={ECC:12, Xid:79} window=5m action_recommendation=cordon+drain tags=[gpu:rtx-a6000]\n
maya: Ideally want automated cordon+drain, but we should avoid mass collateral. current spare GPU capacity: 8/80 (10%).
devon: +1 to cordon, but impose concurrency limits. don't want more than 1 node drained concurrently in the same rack/zone. also prefer graceful drain for long jobs.
lee: reminder: this fleet runs mixed workloads (k8s pods + Slurm). cordon semantics differ. how do we handle Slurm jobs that are running on that node?
alex: proposed lightweight runbook (for review):
```
# k8s path
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector='interruptible=true' --grace-period=120
# Slurm path
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-7 State=DRAIN Reason="auto-quarantine:ECC-spike"
# optional: tag for replacement
kubectl label node gpu-node-7 maintenance=auto-quarantine
```
keep drain conservative: try to reschedule only interruptible workloads, give long-running jobs an N-minute warning before preemption.

devon: also add hysteresis: require either ECC > 10 in 5m OR 3 Xid events within 10m, and require confirmation from the deduped alert (i.e., two distinct detectors). this reduces flapping.
maya: agree. we should also annotate nodes with a TTL tag so autoscaler doesn't tear down replacement too soon: `gpu.health/autoquarantine_ttl=72h`.

lee: for Slurm, instead of immediate requeue we should mark Node as DRAIN then run `scontrol requeue` for checkpointable jobs. non-checkpointable jobs should be left until maintenance window or politely signaled.

tara: worried about autoscaler churn — if we cordon+drain a preemptible node and autoscaler spins up a on-demand replacement, monthly unit costs jump. propose we: 1) throttle replacements per zone, 2) prefer spare pool allocation over on-demand, 3) pause aggressive scale-down for 30m after auto-quarantine.

infra-bot: automation note: scheduling cordon job in 2m for gpu-node-7, policy=conservative, concurrent_drain_limit=1, slack_channel=eng-infra. If conditions clear before action, action will be aborted. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

devon: ops checklist for the automation PR:
- add concurrency limiter keyed by zone
- implement hysteresis (3 Xid in 10m OR ECC>10 in 5m)
- ensure slurm path honors `checkpoint=true` job attr
- add node tag `gpu.health/autoquarantine` + TTL
- pause cluster scale-down for 30m after quarantine

maya: small UX ask: when infra-bot schedules a drain, post expected capacity impact and which pods/jobs will be evicted. can we include an estimate? :eyes:

alex: we can run a dry-run to compute impact before committing to cordon. automation will post a summary with estimated free_gpus and list of affected pods/jobs.

lee: also add alert dedupe/rate-limit: no more than one page per-node per-15m; duplicate alerts should be rolled up to a single incident.

devon: I'll draft the PR and a short runbook snippet for on-call (how to abort, how to force-replace node, telemetry to check). will ping infra-sre for capacity window sign-off. :shipit:
maya: thanks — please include a sample command to force-replace the node in the runbook.

alex: sample force-replace commands for runbook:
```
# mark for immediate replacement
kubectl label node gpu-node-7 replacement=now
# cordon + drain force
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --force --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
# for slurm
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-7 State=DOWN Reason="force-replace"
```

infra-bot: action scheduled: cordon(gpu-node-7) at 1778005230. Will post updates. :bell:
maya: ok closing thread for now. followups in PR comments.
